title: Why Fees Jump: Limits Explained Simply | Engineering Mathematics Ep 1
description:
Rohan pays nothing for his lunch delivery. Fatima, just two hundred metres further away, pays thirty rupees. Is that fair? In this animated lesson we meet Dabba Dash, a food-ordering app built by a computer science student in Pune, and use its delivery fee to understand functions, limits and continuity.

You will see what a function is (one input, exactly one output) with its domain and range, the first careful definition of a limit from Augustin-Louis Cauchy's Cours d'analyse (1821), and a live zoom into the fee graph as the distance gets closer and closer to 2 km from the left and from the right. We look at a formula that breaks at one point, (x squared minus 1) divided by (x minus 1), and see why its limit is still 2. Then we run the three checks for continuity, fix the fee so it has no jump, and see these ideas at work today in a bank, a hospital and income tax slabs. We also look at the human side honestly: real life moves in steps, and in 1872 Karl Weierstrass showed a curve with no breaks that is jagged everywhere.

This is Episode 1 of our Engineering Mathematics series for B.E. and B.Tech computer science students. Fees and distances in the story are example figures.
